Study Area Selection & Global Palm Oil Context

Why this area was audited: Pelalawan Regency, Riau Province, lies along the Kampar Peninsula peat swamp hydrological unit, one of Southeast Asia's most ecologically critical carbon sink landscapes. Auditing this 123.64-hectare concession evaluates commercial oil palm expansion at the boundary between historical estates and deep peat forest.

Multi-Sensor Ground Truth: Google Forest Data Partnership (model_2026a) confirms oil palm presence across established blocks reaching 99.59% peak certainty, while detecting zero crop canopy in the freshly bulldoze-scarred post-2020 clearing zones.

Acute Post-Cutoff Clearing: High-resolution multi-temporal satellite sensors confirm that 26.71 hectares of standing tropical peat forest were clear-felled between 2021 and 2024 to expand commercial oil palm blocks.

Cartographic Interpretation & Multi-Sensor Findings

Figure 1 Evidence: Hansen GFC v1.13 and Sentinel-2 optical composites detect 26.71 ha of severe canopy destruction across four distinct contiguous clear-cuts inside the holding post-December 31, 2020.

Figure 2 Evidence: Rendered in the official Earth Engine emerald-to-lime palette, Google FDP maps established oil palm groves (mean 37.18%, peak 99.59%), with cleared peat corridors awaiting sapling planting.

Statutory Breach: Under EUDR Article 3(a), the presence of post-cutoff deforestation establishes an irremediable strict-liability ban on importing crude palm oil originating from this parcel into the EU.
